originalTitle: Goldman says investors are looking for 'profitable' Chinese business growth overseas
summary: Sluggish consumer demand in China has pushed many companies, such as electric car brands, to accelerate plans for entering other countries.
content:
BEIJING — Equity investors are skeptical of Chinese companies' rapid expansion overseas, according to Goldman Sachs.

The "market wants to look for profitable expansions," Trina Chen, co-head of Greater China equity research at Goldman Sachs Research, said on a podcast that the investment bank published Tuesday.

Sluggish consumer demand in China has pushed many companies, such as electric car brands, to accelerate plans for entering other countries. Automaker Geely is one of the latest Chinese companies to push further abroad, announcing Friday it plans to enter Canada next year .

Chinese companies' overseas market share will likely reach 31% by 2035, up from around 18%, Chen and her team predicted in a Sept. 14 report. Their analysis covered more than 10 sectors, including express delivery, industrial robots and so-called white goods such as air conditioners.

Chinese businesses often find higher profit margins abroad than they would at home, enabling the companies to charge lower prices than local competitors.

Investors need to be convinced the global expansion "does not end up with something similar to involution, where the price actually gets killed because of competition," Chen said Tuesday, adding that geopolitics and market access restrictions also weighs on stock performance.

Involution refers to race-to-the-bottom competition in China, which regulators have attempted to address in recent years.

That uncertainty means Chinese companies have very little of their global expansion opportunity priced into their stocks, Chen said.

But on the flip side, she noted that investors are "ruthless" when incumbent companies lose their market share: A 10% to 15% loss could shrink market capitalization by 50% to 80%.

The Chinese players are not just looking at the U.S. and Europe. Goldman Sachs noted some of the most rapid growth is in emerging markets, as the businesses also pursue areas underserved by competitors.

"Chinese brands are no longer simply market challengers," Euromonitor said in a report last month. "Brands are becoming long-term, embedded competitors capable of reshaping market dynamics across Latin America.
chineseTitle: 高盛表示投资者正在寻求海外“盈利”的中国业务增长
chineseSummary: 中国消费需求疲软促使电动汽车品牌等许多公司加快了进军其他国家的计划。
chineseContent:
北京——高盛表示，股权投资者对中国企业在海外的快速扩张持怀疑态度。

高盛研究部大中华区股票研究联席主管 Trina Chen 在该投行周二发布的播客中表示，“市场希望寻求有利可图的扩张”。

中国消费需求疲软促使电动汽车品牌等许多公司加快了进军其他国家的计划。汽车制造商吉利是最新进军海外市场的中国公司之一，周五宣布计划明年进入加拿大。

陈和她的团队在 9 月 14 日的一份报告中预测，到 2035 年，中国企业的海外市场份额可能会从 18% 左右上升到 31%。他们的分析涵盖了10多个行业，包括快递、工业机器人和空调等所谓的白色家电。

中国企业在国外的利润率往往比在国内高，这使得它们能够比当地竞争对手收取更低的价格。

陈周二表示，投资者需要确信全球扩张“最终不会导致类似于内卷化的结果，即价格实际上因竞争而被扼杀”。他补充说，地缘政治和市场准入限制也会影响股票表现。

内卷化是指中国的逐底竞争，监管机构近年来试图解决这一问题。

陈说，这种不确定性意味着中国企业的全球扩张机会几乎没有反映在其股票中。

但另一方面，她指出，当现有公司失去市场份额时，投资者是“无情的”：10%至15%的损失可能会使市值缩水50%至80%。

中国企业不仅仅着眼于美国和欧洲。高盛指出，增长最快的地区是新兴市场，因为这些企业也在开拓竞争对手服务不足的领域。

欧睿国际在上个月的一份报告中表示：“中国品牌不再只是市场挑战者。” “品牌正在成为长期的、嵌入的竞争对手，能够重塑整个拉丁美洲的市场动态。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
